text:
anya: quick follow-up from the canary RFC — I sketched a probe/oracle proposal for automatic fallback that tries to be conservative but testable. attaching the gist inline.

mike: looks good as a starting point. can you summarize the main safety tradeoffs? :thinking_face:

anya: sure — 3 big ones: 1) sampling vs signal latency (more sampling = faster detection but extra cost/latency), 2) strict thresholds lead to false positives during noise, 3) tie-breaking when multiple metrics disagree (accuracy vs latency vs error-rate).

olivia: about tie-breaking — prefer a prioritized policy (accuracy > correctness > latency) with a decay window. if accuracy regresses consistently for 2 windows we trigger fallback.

chao: we should formalize "window" and "consistency" in the config API so Dedicated / Hosted enforce the same semantics. e.g. rollouts.proto should expose probe_window_s, consecutive_fail_windows, severity.

anya: agreed. draft config snippet: 
```
canary_policy {
  probe_type: "latency,accuracy,exceptions"
  probe_window_s: 60
  check_frequency_s: 15
  consecutive_fail_windows: 2
  severity_priority: ["accuracy","exceptions","latency"]
  abort_action: "fallback_to_model:v1-quantized"
}
```

mike: where does the decision run? control plane only, or local runtime fallback? we saw control-plane delays in region failovers before.

anya: two-layer: primary control-plane decision + local runtime sanity checks. control plane emits decision events (canary_id/state) and a short signed decision token. runtime will accept token or run local fast-checks when network to control-plane is unhealthy.

deploy-bot: [system] canary start event: canary_id=cn-20240315-21 env=prod region=us-west1

olivia: signed-token idea is good — add TTL and audit fields so runtime can verify expiry and why it chose fallback. also include observed-metrics snapshot hash for replay/debug.

chao: tradeoff: signed token increases coupling. alternative: runtime has a compact decision logic param (same proto) that can be pushed as a difffed config, so it can autonomously evaluate if control plane is unreachable.

anya: exactly — control plane authoritative, runtime as failover. we need a clear interface: 
- Control plane -> POST /canary/decision { canary_id, action, token, metadata }
- Runtime receives token, validates signature, applies action immediately.
- If no token and control-plane unreachable, runtime evaluates local policy using pushed compact_policy proto.

sarah: how do we avoid cascade rollback storms? e.g., multiple machines rollback at slightly different times causing capacity spikes.

mike: we add jittered cooldowns and a cluster-level coordinator tag. fallback actions should go through a cluster gate that smooths rollbacks: gate keeps counter, max_concurrent_rollbacks, and staggers actions by random(0,gate_cooldown_s).

anya: also recommend a "soft-fallback" state: redirect a percentage of traffic to fallback model (traffic_split = 20%) for one window before full rollback. helps with noisy spikes.

olivia: observability hooks: every decision should emit a compact event to logs and a full snapshot to S3 for postmortem. link the canary_id to traces and eval sets.

chao: testing: add a canary-sim harness that replays production traces with injected noise. we should run it in CI for canary policy changes.

anya: next steps: 1) I'll open a small RFC PR with the proto + runtime interface, 2) olivia + chao pair on token design and gate logic, 3) mike + sarah build CI harness prototype.

mike: ack. can we add a tiny decision-state machine diagram in the RFC? helps on-call.

anya: yep. will include state transitions: START -> OBSERVE -> SOFT-FALLBACK -> FULL-FALLBACK -> RECOVER -> ROLLOUT.

olivia: nit: add a manual override label and require human ack for production full-fallback if severity==high.

anya: noted. thanks all. I'll drop the PR link here once it's opened. :thumbsup:
